## Dependency graph

```text
Wave 1:  T1 Native atomic batch persistence     T4 Browser import API
                 |                                      |
Wave 2:  T2 ICS conversion coordinator           T5 Calendar import UI
                 |
Wave 3:  T3 Authenticated HTTP endpoint
                 \                                      /
Wave 4:                  T6 Integrated E2E + docs
```

Executable dependency form:

```text
T1 -> T2 -> T3 -> T6
T4 -> T5 -------> T6
```

T1 and T4 may run in parallel because their write scopes are disjoint and their
shared contract is fixed in the approved architecture and program design. T2 and
T5 may also run in parallel after their respective prerequisites. T3 stays on
the backend chain because it consumes T2's error and summary types. T6 begins
only when both tracks are complete.

## T1 — Atomically create a native event batch

- Outcome: `EventService` can create multiple ordinary or recurring native
  events and their occurrence exceptions as one authorized, audited transaction.
- Depends on: none
- Scope: `backend/src/event.rs`; initial batch-persistence cases in
  `backend/tests/ics_import.rs`
- Changes: Add the approved `EventCreateBatch`, item, exception, recurrence-key,
  and result types; implement `EventService::create_batch`; reuse existing event
  validation, recurrence validation, authorization, audit, CalDAV change, and
  notification-replanner helpers; add focused service tests for atomic rollback,
  exception persistence, side-effect counts, and native editability.
- Out of scope: ICS parsing or UID grouping, HTTP routes, parser error mapping,
  rate-limit classification, frontend work.
- Acceptance: A valid mixed batch commits all top-level events and exceptions;
  invalid input or a database failure commits none; authorization is checked as
  `CreateEvent`; every top-level row has one create audit and CalDAV change;
  imported-style rows have no external mapping and remain editable; notification
  replanning occurs only after commit.
- Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml --locked --test ics_import ics_import_batch`
- Handoff: Stable batch input/result types and proven transactional semantics for
  the ICS coordinator; record exact type names if implementation-required Rust
  adjustments preserve the approved meanings.

## T2 — Convert an ICS file into a native event batch

- Outcome: Bounded valid ICS bytes become native event batches with preserved
  standalone, all-day, timed, recurrence-exclusion, and detached-override
  semantics.
- Depends on: T1
- Scope: new `backend/src/ics_import.rs`, `backend/src/lib.rs`, recurrence and
  parser-limit cases in `backend/tests/ics_import.rs`
- Changes: Add `IcsImportService`, import constants, summary, and errors; invoke
  the existing parser with the 1,000-event policy; normalize status and timing;
  group components by UID; attach `EXDATE` and `RECURRENCE-ID` values; reject
  orphan, mismatched, conflicting, unknown-status, malformed, duplicate, and
  over-limit input before persistence; delegate once to `create_batch`; export
  the module.
- Out of scope: HTTP body/media-type handling, route mounting, rate limiting,
  browser API or UI, changes to external-feed ingestion or the generic parser.
- Acceptance: Timed and all-day standalone events import with correct fields;
  a recurring master stores deletions and replacements under the correct keys;
  every semantic or parser failure maps to the approved error category and
  leaves all persistence tables unchanged; re-import creates another editable
  native copy; summary counts top-level events separately from exceptions.
- Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml --locked --test ics_import ics_import_service`
- Handoff: Callable `IcsImportService::import`, stable summary/error contract,
  content-free failure categories, and tested constants for T3.

## T3 — Expose the authenticated, limited import endpoint

- Outcome: Authorized callers can POST raw `text/calendar` bytes and receive the
  approved summary or stable safe error codes through the production router.
- Depends on: T2
- Scope: `backend/src/http.rs`, `backend/src/rate_limiter.rs`, HTTP and role cases
  in `backend/tests/ics_import.rs`
- Changes: Mount and implement `POST
  /api/v1/calendars/:calendar_id/import-ics`; verify media type and non-empty
  body; call `IcsImportService`; map errors; emit content-free structured timing
  logs; classify the route as Standard write rate; add authenticated role,
  response-envelope, media-type, 1 MiB limit, and classifier tests.
- Out of scope: service conversion rules, database schema, frontend behavior,
  application-state or router-builder signature expansion.
- Acceptance: Owner, manager, and editor receive 201 for valid input; viewer,
  free/busy viewer, and unrelated caller receive non-enumerating 404; malformed
  and limit failures expose only their stable codes; incorrect media type and
  empty input are 400; oversized input is 413; the route is Standard-rate
  limited; logs contain no calendar content, UID, filename, title, description,
  or location.
- Verify: `cargo test --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml --locked ics_import`
- Handoff: Final backend endpoint contract and complete integration-test evidence
  for the browser and E2E packets.

## T4 — Add the typed browser import API

- Outcome: Frontend callers can upload a `File` as raw calendar content and
  receive typed counts or a safe typed failure code.
- Depends on: none
- Scope: `frontend/src/calendar/api.ts`, `frontend/src/calendar/api.test.ts`
- Changes: Add `IcsImportSummary`, error-code type,
  `IcsImportApiError`, and `importIcs`; send the `File` body with the approved
  media type; parse only `error.code`; fall back safely for malformed or unknown
  error responses; add focused request/response tests.
- Out of scope: Dialog state, card permissions, file prevalidation, styling,
  backend implementation.
- Acceptance: The client uses the exact approved route, method, content type, and
  unmodified `File` body; successful counts are returned; recognized codes are
  typed; unknown bodies never surface server-provided text.
- Verify: `pnpm --dir frontend test -- api.test.ts`
- Handoff: Stable `importIcs` function, summary, and safe error class for T5.

## T5 — Deliver the accessible calendar import flow

- Outcome: Owners, managers, and editors can select, validate, upload, and
  acknowledge an ICS import from an active calendar card.
- Depends on: T4
- Scope: `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.tsx`,
  `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.css`,
  `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.test.tsx`
- Changes: Add the event-creation permission helper and per-card import action;
  implement the import dialog and its file-size/extension validation, pending,
  success, safe-error, Escape, focus, and access-change behavior; style it using
  existing calendar-dialog conventions; add all approved component tests.
- Out of scope: Backend changes, event-list refresh mechanics, calendar creation
  during import, preview or event selection, E2E fixture.
- Acceptance: Only active detail-access owner/manager/editor cards show Import;
  editors gain no management controls; invalid local files make no request;

  copy without backend text; access denial refreshes calendars; Escape and close
  restore focus to the correct card.
- Verify: `pnpm --dir frontend test -- CalendarManagement.test.tsx`
- Handoff: Completed visible flow and selectors/accessibility names needed by the
  E2E packet.

## T6 — Prove the integrated user journey and document it

- Outcome: A browser-level test proves a real ICS file becomes editable native
  events, and public project documentation describes the new capability.
- Depends on: T3, T5
- Scope: new `e2e/support/import.ics`,
  `e2e/tests/desktop-mvp.spec.ts`, `README.md`, final integrated verification
- Changes: Add the deterministic two-event fixture; drive the visible import
  dialog; assert the success count; verify both events through the API as native

  full relevant checks and fix only regressions caused by this feature.
- Out of scope: Expanding import behavior, deduplication, provider connections,

- Acceptance: The desktop E2E flow imports one timed and one all-day event and
  proves they are not external/read-only; README clearly distinguishes one-time
  import from feed subscription; backend and frontend suites, formatting,
  linting, typechecking, build, and the focused E2E test pass together.
- Verify: `pnpm --dir e2e test -- desktop-mvp.spec.ts --project=desktop`
- Handoff: Final test evidence, any environment-specific E2E notes, and confirmation
  that all six packet acceptance conditions pass together.

## Slice-fit review

### T1

- One outcome and one seam: native batch persistence.
- Binary proof: commit-all/rollback-all plus side-effect assertions.
- Lands working without exposing an unused route.

### T2

- One outcome and one uncertain boundary: normalized ICS to native batch.
- Parser and recurrence policy are local to the new coordinator.
- Binary proof: semantic conversion and zero-write failure cases.

### T3

- One outcome and one seam: authenticated HTTP exposure.
- Consumes stable T2 interfaces; makes no product decisions.
- Binary proof: status, error code, access matrix, body limit, and rate tier.

### T4

- One outcome and one seam: typed browser transport.
- Fully disjoint from backend writes and independently testable.
- Binary proof: exact request and safe response mapping.

### T5

- One user flow: calendar-card import dialog.
- Uses stable T4 interface and existing dialog conventions.
- Binary proof: permission, validation, pending, result, error, and focus tests.

- One outcome: integrated proof and user-facing documentation.
- Contains no new implementation behavior; it verifies both completed tracks.

# Architecture: ICS file import

## Existing seams

### ICS normalization

- `backend/src/ics.rs` already parses an RFC 5545 calendar into
  `NormalizedCalendar` / `NormalizedEvent` values.
- It normalizes timed and all-day values, text fields, status, recurrence rules,
  exclusion dates, detached recurrence instances, sequence, and timestamps.
- `IcsParserLimits` provides bounded component, event, text, and recurrence
  parsing. Its default event limit is 500, so import will use a dedicated limit
  of 1,000 events to match the approved product criterion.
- Parser failures already distinguish malformed input, invalid events, exceeded
  limits, and duplicate `(UID, RECURRENCE-ID)` components without exposing file
  contents.

### Event persistence and authorization

- `backend/src/event.rs` owns native event creation, `CreateEvent`
  authorization, recurrence validation, event audit records, CalDAV change
  records, and notification replanning.
- `CalendarAction::CreateEvent` permits owners, managers, and editors, while
  viewers and free/busy viewers are denied. Inaccessible resources are returned
  as not found to avoid resource enumeration.
- Native events live in `events`; recurring-series overrides and exclusions live
  in `event_recurrence_exceptions`.
- External feed ingestion in `backend/src/external_feed.rs` is not a suitable
  write path. It creates `external_event_mapping` rows, makes events read-only,
  and reconciles them on later refreshes.

### HTTP and browser UI

- Authenticated calendar and event routes are assembled in

coordinator from using the external-feed mapping model.

create new native rows per the approved product behavior.

- Do not log calendar contents, titles, descriptions, locations, UIDs, file
  bytes, or local filenames.
- Database errors remain internal; client errors disclose only the stable import

# Program Design: ICS file import

## Change inventory

### Backend production files

#### `backend/src/ics_import.rs` — new

Own import-specific limits, normalize parser errors, assemble recurrence groups,
convert normalized components to native batch inputs, and coordinate the atomic
event-service call. It must not contain SQL or HTTP response construction.

Proposed public surface:

```rust
pub const MAX_ICS_IMPORT_BYTES: usize = 1024 * 1024;
pub const MAX_ICS_IMPORT_EVENTS: usize = 1_000;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct IcsImportService {
    event_service: EventService,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct IcsImportSummary {
    pub imported_events: usize,
    pub imported_exceptions: usize,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum IcsImportError {
    InvalidCalendar,
    LimitExceeded,
    NotFound,
    Database(sqlx::Error),
}

impl IcsImportService {
    pub fn new(event_service: EventService) -> Self;

    pub async fn import(
        &self,
        actor_user_id: i64,
        is_superadmin: bool,
        calendar_id: i64,
        bytes: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<IcsImportSummary, IcsImportError>;
}
```

Private design types group one top-level component with its `EXDATE` values and
detached `RECURRENCE-ID` components before creating `EventCreateBatch`. Group by
UID without persisting it. Map parser `LimitExceeded` separately; all other
parser and recurrence-relationship failures become `InvalidCalendar`.

Status normalization is fixed: `TENTATIVE` → tentative, `CANCELLED` → cancelled,
and absent or `CONFIRMED` → confirmed. Unknown status values reject the file
instead of silently changing meaning.

#### `backend/src/event.rs`

Add transport-neutral native batch input types:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct EventCreateBatch {
    pub events: Vec<EventCreateItem>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct EventCreateItem {
    pub event: EventMutation,
    pub recurrence_rule: Option<String>,
    pub exceptions: Vec<EventCreateException>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct EventCreateException {
    pub recurrence: EventRecurrenceKey,
    pub replacement: Option<EventMutation>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum EventRecurrenceKey {
    Timed(i64),
    AllDay(String),
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct EventCreateBatchResult {
    pub event_ids: Vec<i64>,
    pub exception_count: usize,
}
```

Add the service method:

```rust
impl EventService {
    pub async fn create_batch(
        &self,
        actor_user_id: i64,
        is_superadmin: bool,
        calendar_id: i64,
        batch: EventCreateBatch,
    ) -> Result<EventCreateBatchResult, EventServiceError>;
}
```

`create_batch` validates the entire batch before beginning a transaction:

- batch is non-empty;
- every mutation passes `validate_mutation`;
- recurrence rules pass `validate_recurrence`;
- exceptions exist only on recurring items;
- recurrence-key kind matches master timing;
- replacement timing kind matches master timing;
- exception keys are unique per item.

Inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, authorize `CreateEvent` once, insert each native
event and its exception rows, reuse `insert_event_audit` with `event.create`, and
reuse `record_caldav_change` with `created`. Commit once, then enqueue each event
ID through the existing notification replanner. Database errors before commit
roll back the entire batch; notification queue pressure after commit does not
change the successful import result, matching single-event create semantics.

Do not write `external_event_mapping` rows. Imported event updates and deletes
must therefore pass the existing `ensure_not_imported` check.

#### `backend/src/http.rs`

- Import `Bytes` and the new import service/error types.
- Mount `POST /api/v1/calendars/:calendar_id/import-ics` whenever
  `event_service` is present.
- Add the handler:

```rust
async fn import_ics(
    State(state): State<ApplicationState>,
    Extension(session): Extension<AuthenticatedSession>,
    Path(calendar_id): Path<i64>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
    body: Bytes,
) -> Result<impl IntoResponse, ApiError>;
```

The handler requires a `text/calendar` media type while tolerating parameters
such as `charset=utf-8`, rejects an empty body, constructs
`IcsImportService::new(event_service)`, times the operation, returns
`(StatusCode::CREATED, Json(summary))`, and emits content-free structured
success/failure events.

Add:

```rust
fn map_ics_import_error(error: IcsImportError) -> ApiError;
```

Map `InvalidCalendar` to `400 / invalid_calendar_file`, `LimitExceeded` to
`400 / calendar_import_limit_exceeded`, inaccessible calendars to the standard
404 response, and database errors to the standard internal response after a
content-free server log.

No `ApplicationState` or router-builder signature changes are needed: the
handler derives the coordinator from the already configured `EventService`.

#### `backend/src/rate_limiter.rs`

Classify `POST .../calendars/:id/import-ics` as `RateLimitTier::Standard` before
the broader permissive calendar-route rules. Add a focused classifier test for
the literal runtime path and parameterized test path.

#### `backend/src/lib.rs`

Export `pub mod ics_import;`.

### Frontend production files

#### `frontend/src/calendar/api.ts`

Add:

```ts
export interface IcsImportSummary {
  imported_events: number;
  imported_exceptions: number;
}

export type IcsImportErrorCode =
  | "invalid_calendar_file"
  | "calendar_import_limit_exceeded"
  | "unknown";

export class IcsImportApiError extends CalendarApiError {
  constructor(status: number, readonly code: IcsImportErrorCode);
}

export async function importIcs(
  api: ApiClient,
  calendarId: number,
  file: File,
): Promise<IcsImportSummary>;
```

Send the `File` itself as the request body with `content-type: text/calendar;
charset=utf-8`. On error, parse only `error.code` from the standard envelope and
fall back to `unknown`; never display a server-provided message directly.

#### `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.tsx`

Add `canCreateEvents(calendar)` for owner, manager, and editor detail-access
roles. Keep `canManage` unchanged for settings, ACL, and archival actions.

Extend `CalendarCard` with an import callback and trigger ref. Show **Import
ICS** only for active calendars satisfying `canCreateEvents`.

Add an `IcsImportDialog` component with this contract:

```ts
interface IcsImportDialogProps {
  api: ApiClient;
  calendar: Calendar;
  onClose(): void;
  triggerEl: HTMLButtonElement | null;
}
```

The dialog owns selected file, submitting state, success summary, and safe error
text. It accepts `.ics,text/calendar`, validates extension and `file.size <=
1_048_576`, disables Import until valid, prevents resubmission while pending,
supports Escape only while not submitting, focuses its close control on open,
and restores focus to its own triggering button on close.

Success remains visible inside the dialog until the person acknowledges it;
there is no calendar-list reload because event data is loaded by the calendar
view, not `CalendarManagement`.

#### `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.css`

Add styles for the import card action, file field, limit/help text, progress,
error, and success states. Reuse existing modal/dialog spacing, buttons, focus
ring, and narrow-viewport conventions rather than introducing another visual
system.

### Documentation

#### `README.md`

Add one feature bullet for one-time editable ICS file import and add the import
route to the API overview. Keep it distinct from external ICS feed subscription.

### Test and fixture files

#### `backend/tests/ics_import.rs` — new

Service and HTTP integration coverage using a migrated temporary SQLite database
and authenticated router:

- `imports_timed_and_all_day_components_as_editable_native_events` — response
  counts are correct; all fields and timezone/date columns are stored; no
  `external_event_mapping` rows exist; a later native update succeeds.
- `imports_recurrence_exclusions_and_detached_overrides` — one master is stored,
  deleted and replacement exception rows have correct recurrence keys, and
  expanded reads omit/move the intended occurrences.
- `rejects_orphan_or_kind_mismatched_detached_instances_atomically` — returns
  `invalid_calendar_file` and leaves `events`, exceptions, audits, and CalDAV
  changes unchanged.
- `rejects_malformed_duplicate_and_over_limit_files_atomically` — stable error
  codes distinguish invalid input from limits and no rows are committed.
- `allows_owner_manager_and_editor_but_hides_denials_as_not_found` — all three
  writers receive 201; viewer, free/busy viewer, and unrelated user receive 404.
- `reimport_creates_a_second_native_copy` — approved duplicate behavior is
  explicit and both copies remain editable.
- `creates_audit_and_caldav_records_for_each_top_level_event` — counts and action
  names match ordinary event creation, while exceptions do not create extra
  top-level records.
- `requires_text_calendar_and_enforces_the_application_body_limit` — incorrect
  media type is 400 and a body over 1 MiB is 413.

Use small inline ICS strings for semantic tests; generate limit cases in test
code so a large fixture is not committed.

#### `backend/src/rate_limiter.rs` tests

- `ics_import_is_standard_write_rate` — POST import is Standard; GET and nearby
  calendar management routes retain their existing classification.

#### `frontend/src/calendar/api.test.ts`

- `posts_raw_ics_file_and_returns_import_counts` — exact route, POST method,
  `text/calendar` content type, and `File` body.
- `maps_import_error_codes_without_exposing_server_messages` — recognized and
  unknown envelopes become typed safe errors.

#### `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.test.tsx`

- `offers_import_to_owner_manager_and_editor_only` — editor gains import without
  gaining edit/share/archive controls; viewer, free/busy, and archived cards do
  not expose import.
- `validates_the_selected_ics_file_before_upload` — extension and 1 MiB errors
  are local and make no request.
- `uploads_once_and_reports_the_imported_event_count` — second submit is disabled
  while pending and success remains until acknowledgement.
- `shows_safe_messages_for_invalid_limit_and_unknown_failures` — stable codes map
  to actionable copy; backend message text is absent.
- `closes_import_with_escape_and_restores_the_correct_trigger` — dialog keyboard
  and per-card focus behavior match the sharing flow.
- `refreshes_calendar_access_after_an_import_denial` — 401/403/404 access change
  closes stale controls and refreshes the calendar list.

#### `e2e/support/import.ics` — new

A deterministic two-event file containing one timed event and one all-day event
with dates inside the E2E query window. Content must be independent from the
existing remote-feed fixture.

#### `e2e/tests/desktop-mvp.spec.ts`

Extend the authenticated desktop flow to navigate to calendar management,
import the fixture through the visible dialog, assert the “2 events imported”
result, then query the event API and prove the imported events are native and
editable (`read_only` / `is_external` are absent or false).

## Main call paths

### Valid upload

```text
CalendarManagement
  -> importIcs(ApiClient, calendarId, File)
  -> POST /api/v1/calendars/:calendar_id/import-ics
  -> import_ics handler
  -> IcsImportService::import
  -> ics::parse_calendar(import limits)
  -> recurrence grouping + EventCreateBatch conversion
  -> EventService::create_batch
  -> authorize CreateEvent
  -> events + recurrence exceptions + audit + CalDAV changes (one transaction)
  -> commit
  -> notification replanner per top-level event
  -> IcsImportSummary
  -> success dialog
```

```text
bytes / parser / recurrence grouping
  -> IcsImportError::{InvalidCalendar | LimitExceeded}
  -> stable ApiError code
  -> IcsImportApiError
  -> safe dialog copy
  -> zero database writes
```

### Authorization race

```text
visible import action from stale calendar list
  -> EventService::create_batch authorizes inside write transaction
  -> 404
  -> isCalendarAccessChange
  -> close dialog + reload calendars + access-changed message
```

# Program Design: ICS file import

## Change inventory

### Backend production files

#### `backend/src/ics_import.rs` — new

Own import-specific limits, normalize parser errors, assemble recurrence groups,
convert normalized components to native batch inputs, and coordinate the atomic
event-service call. It must not contain SQL or HTTP response construction.

Proposed public surface:

```rust
pub const MAX_ICS_IMPORT_BYTES: usize = 1024 * 1024;
pub const MAX_ICS_IMPORT_EVENTS: usize = 1_000;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct IcsImportService {
    event_service: EventService,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct IcsImportSummary {
    pub imported_events: usize,
    pub imported_exceptions: usize,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum IcsImportError {
    InvalidCalendar,
    LimitExceeded,
    NotFound,
    Database(sqlx::Error),
}

impl IcsImportService {
    pub fn new(event_service: EventService) -> Self;

    pub async fn import(
        &self,
        actor_user_id: i64,
        is_superadmin: bool,
        calendar_id: i64,
        bytes: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<IcsImportSummary, IcsImportError>;
}
```

Private design types group one top-level component with its `EXDATE` values and
detached `RECURRENCE-ID` components before creating `EventCreateBatch`. Group by
UID without persisting it. Map parser `LimitExceeded` separately; all other
parser and recurrence-relationship failures become `InvalidCalendar`.

Status normalization is fixed: `TENTATIVE` → tentative, `CANCELLED` → cancelled,
and absent or `CONFIRMED` → confirmed. Unknown status values reject the file
instead of silently changing meaning.

#### `backend/src/event.rs`

Add transport-neutral native batch input types:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct EventCreateBatch {
    pub events: Vec<EventCreateItem>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct EventCreateItem {
    pub event: EventMutation,
    pub recurrence_rule: Option<String>,
    pub exceptions: Vec<EventCreateException>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct EventCreateException {
    pub recurrence: EventRecurrenceKey,
    pub replacement: Option<EventMutation>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum EventRecurrenceKey {
    Timed(i64),
    AllDay(String),
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct EventCreateBatchResult {
    pub event_ids: Vec<i64>,
    pub exception_count: usize,
}
```

Add the service method:

```rust
impl EventService {
    pub async fn create_batch(
        &self,
        actor_user_id: i64,
        is_superadmin: bool,
        calendar_id: i64,
        batch: EventCreateBatch,
    ) -> Result<EventCreateBatchResult, EventServiceError>;
}
```

`create_batch` validates the entire batch before beginning a transaction:

- batch is non-empty;
- every mutation passes `validate_mutation`;
- recurrence rules pass `validate_recurrence`;
- exceptions exist only on recurring items;
- recurrence-key kind matches master timing;
- replacement timing kind matches master timing;
- exception keys are unique per item.

Inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, authorize `CreateEvent` once, insert each native
event and its exception rows, reuse `insert_event_audit` with `event.create`, and
reuse `record_caldav_change` with `created`. Commit once, then enqueue each event
ID through the existing notification replanner. Database errors before commit
roll back the entire batch; notification queue pressure after commit does not
change the successful import result, matching single-event create semantics.

Do not write `external_event_mapping` rows. Imported event updates and deletes
must therefore pass the existing `ensure_not_imported` check.

#### `backend/src/http.rs`

- Import `Bytes` and the new import service/error types.
- Mount `POST /api/v1/calendars/:calendar_id/import-ics` whenever
  `event_service` is present.
- Add the handler:

```rust
async fn import_ics(
    State(state): State<ApplicationState>,
    Extension(session): Extension<AuthenticatedSession>,
    Path(calendar_id): Path<i64>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
    body: Bytes,
) -> Result<impl IntoResponse, ApiError>;
```

The handler requires a `text/calendar` media type while tolerating parameters
such as `charset=utf-8`, rejects an empty body, constructs
`IcsImportService::new(event_service)`, times the operation, returns
`(StatusCode::CREATED, Json(summary))`, and emits content-free structured
success/failure events.

Add:

```rust
fn map_ics_import_error(error: IcsImportError) -> ApiError;
```

Map `InvalidCalendar` to `400 / invalid_calendar_file`, `LimitExceeded` to
`400 / calendar_import_limit_exceeded`, inaccessible calendars to the standard
404 response, and database errors to the standard internal response after a
content-free server log.

No `ApplicationState` or router-builder signature changes are needed: the
handler derives the coordinator from the already configured `EventService`.

#### `backend/src/rate_limiter.rs`

Classify `POST .../calendars/:id/import-ics` as `RateLimitTier::Standard` before
the broader permissive calendar-route rules. Add a focused classifier test for
the literal runtime path and parameterized test path.

#### `backend/src/lib.rs`

Export `pub mod ics_import;`.

### Frontend production files

#### `frontend/src/calendar/api.ts`

Add:

```ts
export interface IcsImportSummary {
  imported_events: number;
  imported_exceptions: number;
}

export type IcsImportErrorCode =
  | "invalid_calendar_file"
  | "calendar_import_limit_exceeded"
  | "unknown";

export class IcsImportApiError extends CalendarApiError {
  constructor(status: number, readonly code: IcsImportErrorCode);
}

export async function importIcs(
  api: ApiClient,
  calendarId: number,
  file: File,
): Promise<IcsImportSummary>;
```

Send the `File` itself as the request body with `content-type: text/calendar;

fall back to `unknown`; never display a server-provided message directly.

```ts
interface IcsImportDialogProps {
  api: ApiClient;
  calendar: Calendar;
  onClose(): void;
  triggerEl: HTMLButtonElement | null;
}
```

The dialog owns selected file, submitting state, success summary, and safe error

supports Escape only while not submitting, focuses its close control on open,
and restores focus to its own triggering button on close.

there is no calendar-list reload because event data is loaded by the calendar
view, not `CalendarManagement`.

#### `frontend/src/calendar/CalendarManagement.css`

Add styles for the import card action, file field, limit/help text, progress,
error, and success states. Reuse existing modal/dialog spacing, buttons, focus

system.

#### `README.md`

Add one feature bullet for one-time editable ICS file import and add the import
route to the API overview. Keep it distinct from external ICS feed subscription.

#### `backend/tests/ics_import.rs` — new

and authenticated router:

- `imports_timed_and_all_day_components_as_editable_native_events` — response
  counts are correct; all fields and timezone/date columns are stored; no

- `imports_recurrence_exclusions_and_detached_overrides` — one master is stored,
  deleted and replacement exception rows have correct recurrence keys, and

- `rejects_orphan_or_kind_mismatched_detached_instances_atomically` — returns

- `rejects_malformed_duplicate_and_over_limit_files_atomically` — stable error

- `allows_owner_manager_and_editor_but_hides_denials_as_not_found` — all three

A deterministic two-event file containing one timed event and one all-day event
